axis.description: alternatives | models. 'alternatives' when the ad names or weighs another way to get the same thing (a studio, a membership, a gym or spa, another kind of sauna, a blanket), even if it also quotes a price; 'models' only when the ad is purely about choosing between, pricing or sizing the tenant's own cabins. It picks the headline formula.

headline.description: axis models: '<Model A> vs <Model B> vs <Model C>: Which <category> Fits <audience>', the three names exactly as facts_pack.comparison.models gives them, in column order. axis alternatives: '<category> vs <alternative>: What <audience> Should Compare', <alternative> one of this page's alternatives. <category> is the product category, never the tenant's name or a model name; <audience> names people by situation or goal (2 to 5 words), never a bare 'people' or 'buyers'. Never a price.

dek.description: One-sentence subhead under the headline. Any number or spec in it cites claim_ids.

hero.description: The header's hero image: the featured model, one asset_id from facts_pack.assets -- never a model's column image (facts_pack.comparison.models[].image.id).

lifestyle.description: One lifestyle or installation photo from facts_pack.assets, shown between the alternatives and the who-it-is-for section. Different from the hero and from every column image.

extra_rows.description: 1-2 extra table rows worth a look for this ad's angle, each {"id": "<key>"} with key one of facts_pack.comparison.extra_row_options[].key. You pick the row; the renderer fills every cell from verified claims.

best_for.description: Exactly one entry per model, in column order: {"id": "<model id>", "text": "one short line naming who this model suits", "claim_ids": [...]}. Shown under the table. Any number or spec cites that model's own cell claim_ids.

numbers_mean.description: What the numbers mean: exactly 3 short paragraphs (40 to 90 words each) reading the table for a buyer -- space, power, price. Each cites the claim_ids of the cells it reads from.

alternatives.description: 2-3 alternatives the ad names or implies, each id from this schema's own top-level 'alternatives' list. The summary, the similarities and 'theirs' contain NO digits, dollar amounts, percentages or trigger words: nothing verified describes an alternative. 'ours' is the tenant's side and cites claim_ids for any number or spec.

summary.description: One plain sentence on what this alternative is and who picks it.

similarities.description: 2-3 short plain lines on what it shares with owning one.

differences.description: 2-3 differences, each {"theirs": "plain line about the alternative", "ours": {"text": "the tenant's side", "claim_ids": [...]}}.

who_for.description: Who each model is for: exactly one entry per model, in column order, {"id": "<model id>", "text": "2-3 sentences", "claim_ids": [...]}. Name real, checkable fits and limits (room, power, household size, budget), never a fake drawback.

faq.description: 5-7 questions a comparer actually asks, each {"question", "answer" (2-4 sentences), "claim_ids"}. An answer with a number, price, spec or trigger word carries claim_ids.

closing.description: The closing block: an optional short headline and exactly 3 recap bullets. The renderer adds the CTA, the fixed warranty and financing sentences, and the HSA/FSA line when verified -- never write them.

cta_text.description: One of allowed_cta_texts, verbatim. The renderer draws it in the header, the closing block and the phone sticky bar.

cta_url.description: The page's one CTA destination: facts_pack.product.url or the tenant's collection path. Never a second cta_url anywhere.
